title: Every mind different (Berakhot 58a)
hookLine: seeing a great crowd, one blesses the One who knows each heart
tomorrow: who baked your bread before you were even awake?

lines: BLESSED IS THE WISE OF SECRETS.
cards: From the wings of a stage, a full house looks like one thing. A dark shape, a single cough, one big laugh. A stadium does the same, or a packed train at rush hour: the crowd.
So what blessing fits a sea of faces? The Talmud has one ready. When you see a great crowd of Israel, you say: blessed is the Wise of secrets.
And it gives the reason in one breath.

teach.h: NO TWO MINDS, NO TWO FACES.
teach.b: The reason: because their minds are not like one another, and their faces are not like one another. The crowd only looks like one thing from far away.
God, the blessing says, knows the secret inside every one of them, which is exactly what the person watching can't. That's why it's called the Wise of secrets. Now honesty about scope.

This blessing in Berakhot is said over a great crowd of the Jewish people. But the Mishnah, in another tractate, Sanhedrin, says something wider about every human being. Why was humanity created from a single person?

teach.h: ONE ANCESTOR, SO NO ONE RANKS.
teach.b: So that no one could say to another, my ancestor is greater than yours.
And to show God's greatness: a person stamps many coins with one seal and they all come out alike. God stamped every human with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another.
Put the two together, and here's what you could tell a friend tonight. One family, so no one ranks their ancestors above anyone else's.
Every face different, so no one is just part of the blob. Alike enough to be family, different enough that each one is a secret. That's the crowd at a ballgame, a bus stop, a hallway between classes.

how: Jewish law gives a blessing on seeing a great crowd of Jews: 'Blessed… Wise of secrets' (chacham ha-razim); the Mishnah in Sanhedrin 4:5 teaches that every human descends from one person and that no two are alike.

o: every person's mind is closed, so no one can be known
a crowd should agree with one mind before it acts
no two people think alike, and God knows each one

games.q: the crowd and the coin — tap the pairs.
p: blessed is the Wise of secrets
no two minds, no two faces alike
so no one says, my ancestor is greater
all alike; people from one seal, none alike

s: the Talmud's crowd blessing praises God for making people all alike
it praises the Wise of secrets because their minds and faces are not alike.
the Mishnah says humanity began with one person so no one could rank their ancestors
Sanhedrin 4:5: so no one can say, my ancestor is greater than yours.
the Wise of secrets blessing is said over any crowd of any people
in Berakhot it's for a great crowd of Israel; the wider teaching about all people is in Sanhedrin 4:5.

games.q: you're stuck in a packed airport security line and someone mutters, "ugh, these people." what does today's page see in that line?
o: a crowd is a crowd; it's fair to treat it as one big obstacle.
everyone there is basically the same, so no one should complain.
every face different and every mind a secret, all from one family.
games.why: the Talmud blesses the Wise of secrets because no two minds or faces are alike, and the Mishnah says every person comes from one, so no one ranks.

practice: Close your eyes and bring back a crowd you were part of this week: a hallway, a store, a bus. Let three faces come into focus, one at a time. For each, notice: a whole mind I'll never fully see, from the same first family as me.

wordCard.voice: Every mind different: why the Talmud blesses the Wise of secrets over a crowd, the One who knows what no watcher can.

orig.note: Hebrew: Wise of secrets, the name for God in the blessing over a great crowd.

carryVoice: For the next crowd you're in: every mind different, every face from the same first family. Thirty-seven of fifty.

sources.ref: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 58a (one who sees crowds of Israel says 'Blessed… Wise of secrets', for their minds and faces are not alike)
Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (humanity created from one person so no one says 'my ancestor is greater'; one seal, no two alike)
